children: SpaceX (SPCX, Financials), is approaching another major lockup expiration, with about 328 million shares scheduled to become available for sale on Sept. 24.

The unlock could increase the number of shares available for trading if early investors, employees or insiders decide to sell. However, an expiration does not require shareholders to sell, so the actual market impact will depend on trading activity and investor demand.

SpaceX's previous major unlock on Sept. 9 was followed by a 3.9% decline in the stock. Shares have also experienced significant swings since their IPO, initially closing at $161.11, about 19% above the $135 offering price.
The company has additional lockup expirations planned through June 2027, keeping potential share supply on the radar as investors assess the stock's valuation and growth prospects.

Beyond the near-term share unlock, SpaceX investors are watching the company's Starlink, Starship and AI businesses. The company's 14th Starship test flight is scheduled for Sept. 28 and is expected to include the deployment of Starlink V3 satellites.
SPCX shares were down 0.75% in premarket trading ahead of the Sept. 24 unlock.
The next catalyst is how the stock trades as the newly unlocked shares become available, followed by the upcoming Starship test.

title: SpaceX Faces Another Share Unlock as Investors Watch Supply
